translations.idiomatic: " Hearing this, Chang immediately had officials seize Xushun and imprison him; day and night he prosecuted the case until Xushun died in custody.

sentences.zh: 舜當出死，敞使主簿持教告舜曰：「五日京兆竟何如？

translations.literal: When Xushun was about to go out to execution, Chang had his chief clerk hold the order and tell Xushun: "How about that five-day Metropolitan Governor after all?
translations.idiomatic: When Xushun was about to be executed, Chang had his chief clerk bring the order and tell him, "How about that five-day Metropolitan Governor after all?

sentences.zh: 冬月已盡，延命乎？

translations.literal: The winter month is already spent—extending your life, is it?
translations.idiomatic: Winter is nearly over—still extending your life, is it?

sentences.zh: 」乃棄舜市。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he abandoned Xushun at the market.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he had Xushun executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 會立春，行冤獄使者出，舜家載屍並編敞教，自言使者。

translations.literal: It happened to be the Establishment of Spring; the envoy reviewing wrongful imprisonment cases went forth; Xushun's family loaded the corpse together with a copy of Chang's order and themselves told the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: It happened to be the Establishment of Spring, when envoys reviewing wrongful imprisonment went forth; Xushun's family brought the corpse together with a copy of Chang's order and appealed to the envoy.

sentences.zh: 使者奏敞賊殺不辜。

translations.literal: The envoy memorialized that Chang had murdered the innocent as a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy memorialized that Chang had murdered an innocent man.

sentences.zh: 上欲令敞得自便，即先下敞前坐楊惲奏，免為庶人。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to let Chang obtain convenience for himself and first sent down Chang's earlier conviction in the Yang Yun case, dismissing him as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to let Chang go free and first sent down his earlier conviction in the Yang Yun case, dismissing him as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 敞詣闕上印綬，便從闕下亡命。

translations.literal: Chang went to the palace gate and returned his seal and cord, then straightway fled for his life from below the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chang went to the palace gate, returned his seal and cord, and fled for his life from below the gate.

sentences.zh: 數月，京師吏民解馳，枹鼓數起，而翼州部中有大賊，天子思敞功效，使使者即家在所召敞。

translations.literal: Several months later, the capital's officials and people grew slack; drum-beats of alarm repeatedly arose; and in the Jizhou region there was a great bandit—the Son of Heaven thought of Chang's achievements and sent an envoy to summon Chang at his home where he was.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later, law and order in the capital slackened and alarms repeatedly sounded; meanwhile a great bandit arose in the Jizhou region. The emperor recalled Chang's achievements and sent an envoy to summon him at his home.

sentences.zh: 敞身被重劾，及使者至，妻子家室皆泣，惶懼，而敞獨笑曰：「吾身亡命為民，郡吏當就捕。

translations.literal: Chang's person bore heavy impeachments; when the envoy arrived, wife, children, and household all wept in fear and dread, yet Chang alone laughed and said: "I fled for my life on behalf of the people; the commandery officials ought to come and arrest me.
translations.idiomatic: Chang faced serious charges; when the envoy arrived, his wife, children, and household all wept in fear, yet Chang alone laughed and said, "I fled for the people's sake; the commandery officials ought to come and arrest me.

sentences.zh: 今使者來，此天子欲用我也。

translations.literal: Now the envoy has come—this means the Son of Heaven wishes to employ me.
translations.idiomatic: Now the envoy has come—this means the emperor wishes to employ me.

sentences.zh: 」裝隨使者，詣公車上書曰：「臣前幸得備位列卿，待罪京兆，坐殺掾絮舜。

translations.literal: " He packed and followed the envoy, went to the Imperial Carriages Office and submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject before was fortunate to be ranked among the ministers, held office in guilt at the capital metropolis, and sat in judgment for killing clerk Xushun.
translations.idiomatic: " He packed and followed the envoy, went to the Imperial Carriages Office and submitted a memorial: "Your subject was once fortunate to rank among the ministers and served as Metropolitan Governor, where I was convicted of killing clerk Xushun.

sentences.zh: 舜本臣敞素所厚吏，數蒙恩貸。

translations.literal: Xushun was originally an official your subject Chang had long favored, repeatedly receiving grace and leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Xushun was an official I had long favored and repeatedly spared.

sentences.zh: 以臣有章劾當免，受記考事，便歸臥家，謂臣『五日京兆』。

translations.literal: Because your subject had an impeachment memorial and ought to be dismissed, he received a note to examine the case and straightway returned to lie at home, calling your subject 'a five-day Metropolitan Governor.'
translations.idiomatic: When I faced impeachment and ought to be dismissed, he received orders to investigate a case, went straight home, and called me 'a five-day Metropolitan Governor.'

sentences.zh: 背恩忘義，傷薄欲化。

translations.literal: He turned his back on grace and forgot righteousness, injuring shallow desires for transformation.
translations.idiomatic: He turned his back on grace and forgot righteousness, undermining my efforts at reform.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以舜無狀，枉法以誅之。

translations.literal: Your subject privately held that Xushun was without proper form and bent the law to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject held that Xushun was insolent and executed him by bending the law.

sentences.zh: 臣敞賊殺不辜，鞠獄故不直，雖伏明法，死無所恨！

translations.literal: Your subject Chang, murdering the innocent as a bandit, bent the prison examination and therefore was not upright—though he submits to the clear law, in death he has no regret!
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Chang murdered an innocent man and conducted the trial unjustly—though I submit to the clear law, I die without regret!

sentences.zh: 」天子引見敞，拜為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven summoned Chang to audience and appointed him Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor received Chang in audience and appointed him Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 敞到部，盜賊屏跡。

translations.literal: When Chang reached his inspectorate, bandits vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang reached his post, bandits vanished.

sentences.zh: ----3皇太子柔仁好儒，見上所用多文法吏，以刑繩下，嘗侍燕從容言：「陛下持刑太深，宜用儒生。

translations.literal: ----3 The heir apparent was gentle, benevolent, and fond of Confucianism; seeing that those the emperor employed were mostly legalist officials who bound the people with punishments, he once while attending a banquet spoke at ease: "Your Majesty holds punishments too deep; you ought to employ Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 The heir apparent was gentle, benevolent, and fond of Confucianism; seeing that the emperor employed mostly legalist officials who governed by punishments, he once at a banquet said at ease, "Your Majesty applies punishments too harshly; you ought to employ Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 」帝作色曰：「漢家自有制度，本以霸王道雜之。

translations.literal: " The emperor changed countenance and said: "The House of Han has its own institutions, fundamentally mixing the ways of hegemon and king.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's expression changed and he said, "The House of Han has its own institutions, fundamentally mixing the ways of hegemon and king.

sentences.zh: 奈何純任德教，用周政乎！

translations.literal: How can one purely entrust moral teaching and employ Zhou government!
translations.idiomatic: How can one rely purely on moral teaching and employ Zhou government!

sentences.zh: 且俗儒不達時宜，好是古非今，使人眩於名實，不知所守，何足委任！

translations.literal: Moreover vulgar Confucians do not comprehend the timely fit, delight in praising antiquity and condemning the present, and make people dazzled between name and reality, not knowing what to uphold—how are they fit to be entrusted!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover vulgar Confucians do not grasp the times, delight in praising antiquity and condemning the present, and dazzle people between name and reality so they do not know what to uphold—how can they be entrusted!

sentences.zh: 」乃歎曰：「亂我家者，太子也！

translations.literal: " He then sighed and said: "He who will disorder my house is the heir apparent!
translations.idiomatic: " He then sighed and said, "He who will disorder my house is the heir apparent!

sentences.zh: :臣光曰：王霸無異道。

translations.literal: : Minister Guang said: The ways of king and hegemon are not different paths.
translations.idiomatic: : Minister Guang said: The ways of king and hegemon are not different paths.

sentences.zh: 昔三代之隆，禮樂、征伐自天子出，則謂之王。

translations.literal: In antiquity at the height of the Three Dynasties, when rites and music and campaigns and punishments issued from the Son of Heaven, it was called kingship.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity at the height of the Three Dynasties, when rites, music, and campaigns issued from the Son of Heaven, it was called kingship.

sentences.zh: 天子微弱不能治諸侯，諸侯有能率其與國同討不庭以尊王室者，則謂之霸。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven was weak and could not govern the feudal lords, and a feudal lord was able to lead the states allied with him jointly to punish the disobedient and honor the royal house, it was called hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven was weak and could not govern the feudal lords, and a lord was able to lead allied states to punish the disobedient and honor the royal house, it was called hegemony.

sentences.zh: 其所以行之也，皆本仁祖義，任賢使能，賞善罰惡，禁暴誅亂。

translations.literal: The means by which they were carried out all took benevolence as root and righteousness as model, employed the worthy and used the able, rewarded good and punished evil, forbade violence and executed disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The means by which both were carried out all took benevolence as root and righteousness as model, employed the worthy, rewarded good and punished evil, and forbade violence.

sentences.zh: 顧名位有尊卑，德澤有深淺，功業有鉅細，政令有廣狹耳，非若白黑、甘苦之相反也。

translations.literal: Only that name and position had high and low, virtue's favor had deep and shallow, achievements had large and small, and government orders had broad and narrow—that is all; it is not like black and white or sweet and bitter in mutual opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Only that rank had high and low, favor had depth, achievements had scale, and orders had scope—that is all; it is not like black and white or sweet and bitter in opposition.

sentences.zh: 漢之所以不能復三代之治者，由人主之不為，非先王之道不可復行於後世也。

translations.literal: The reason Han could not restore the governance of the Three Dynasties was that the human ruler did not do it—not that the former kings' Way could not again be practiced in later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The reason Han could not restore Three Dynasties governance was that rulers did not do it—not that the former kings' Way could not be practiced again.

sentences.zh: 夫儒有君子，有小人。

translations.literal: Among Confucians there are gentlemen and there are petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Among Confucians there are gentlemen and petty men.

sentences.zh: 彼俗儒者，誠不足與為治也，獨不可求真儒而用之乎？

translations.literal: Those vulgar Confucians truly are not fit to govern with—but can one alone not seek true Confucians and employ them?
translations.idiomatic: Those vulgar Confucians truly are not fit to govern with—but cannot one seek true Confucians and employ them?

sentences.zh: 稷、契、皋陶、伯益、伊尹、周公、孔子，皆大儒也，使漢得而用之，功烈豈若是而止邪！

translations.literal: Ji, Qi, Gao Yao, Bo Yi, Yi Yin, Duke of Zhou, and Confucius were all great Confucians; had Han obtained and employed them, would achievements and glory have stopped like this!
translations.idiomatic: Ji, Qi, Gao Yao, Bo Yi, Yi Yin, Duke of Zhou, and Confucius were all great Confucians; had Han obtained and employed them, would achievements have stopped at this!

sentences.zh: 孝宣謂太子懦而不立，闇於治體，必亂我家，則可矣；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan's saying the heir apparent was weak and could not stand, dark to the body of governance, and would surely disorder his house—that could pass;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan's saying the heir apparent was weak, unfit to stand, ignorant of governance, and would disorder his house—that could pass;

sentences.zh: 乃曰王道不可行，儒者不可用，豈不過甚矣哉！

translations.literal: yet to say the kingly Way could not be practiced and Confucians could not be employed—was that not going too far!
translations.idiomatic: yet to say the kingly Way could not be practiced and Confucians could not be employed—was that not going too far!

sentences.zh: 殆非所以訓示子孫，垂法將來者也。

translations.literal: It was nearly not the means to instruct and show sons and grandsons or to hand down law for the future.
translations.idiomatic: It was hardly the way to instruct posterity or hand down law for the future.

sentences.zh: ----4淮陽憲王好法律，聰達有材；

translations.literal: ----4 Prince Xian of Huaiyang was fond of law, clever and penetrating with talent;
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Prince Xian of Huaiyang was fond of law, clever and talented;

sentences.zh: 王母張婕妤尤幸。

translations.literal: his queen mother, Lady Zhang the Beautiful Companion, was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: his queen mother, Lady Zhang the Beautiful Companion, was especially favored.

sentences.zh: 上由是疏太子而愛淮陽憲王，數嗟歎憲王曰：「真我子也！

translations.literal: The emperor thereby grew distant from the heir apparent and loved Prince Xian of Huaiyang, repeatedly sighing in admiration of the prince and saying: "Truly my son!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereby grew distant from the heir apparent and loved Prince Xian of Huaiyang, repeatedly sighing and saying, "Truly my son!

sentences.zh: 」常有意欲立憲王，然用太子起於微細，上少依倚許氏，及即位而許后以殺死，故弗忍也。

translations.literal: " He constantly had intent to establish Prince Xian, yet because the heir apparent had risen from minute origins and the emperor in youth had relied on the Xu clan, and after accession the Empress Xu died by killing, he therefore could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: " He constantly intended to establish Prince Xian, yet because the heir apparent had risen from humble origins, the emperor in youth had relied on the Xu clan, and after accession Empress Xu died by execution, he could not bear to do it.

sentences.zh: 久之，上拜韋玄成為淮陽中尉，以玄成嘗讓爵于兄，欲以感諭憲王。

translations.literal: After a long time, the emperor appointed Wei Xuancheng as Commandant of Huaiyang, because Xuancheng had once yielded his noble rank to his elder brother, wishing thereby to move and instruct Prince Xian.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, the emperor appointed Wei Xuancheng Commandant of Huaiyang, because Xuancheng had once yielded his noble rank to his elder brother, wishing thereby to instruct Prince Xian by example.

sentences.zh: 由是太子遂安。

translations.literal: Thereby the heir apparent was at last secure.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby the heir apparent was at last secure.

sentences.zh: ----5匈奴呼韓邪單于之敗也，左伊秩訾王為呼韓邪計，勸令稱臣入朝事漢，從漢求助，如此，匈奴乃定。

translations.literal: ----5 When the Xiongnu Chanyu Huhanye was defeated, the Left Yizhi Zhi King made a plan for Huhanye, urging him to declare himself a subject, enter court, and serve Han, follow Han to seek aid—thus the Xiongnu would be settled.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 When Chanyu Huhanye of the Xiongnu was defeated, the Left Yizhi Zhi King advised him to declare himself a subject, attend court, and serve Han, seeking Han's aid—thus the Xiongnu would be settled.

sentences.zh: 呼韓邪問諸大臣，皆曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Huhanye asked the various great ministers; all said: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Huhanye asked the great ministers; all said, "It cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 匈奴之俗，本上氣力而下服役，以馬上戰鬥為國，故有威名於百蠻。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu custom esteems above physical strength and below servitude; taking battle on horseback as the state, therefore they have a prestigious name among the hundred barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongnu custom esteems strength above and servitude below; taking battle on horseback as the foundation of state, they have prestige among the hundred barbarians.

sentences.zh: 戰死，壯士所有也。

translations.literal: To die in battle is what a stalwart man possesses.
translations.idiomatic: To die in battle is a stalwart man's portion.

sentences.zh: 今兄弟爭國，不在兄則在弟，雖死猶有威名，子孫常長諸國。

translations.literal: Now brothers contend for the state—if not the elder brother then the younger; though one dies he still has a prestigious name, and sons and grandsons constantly lead the various states.
translations.idiomatic: Now brothers contend for the state—if not the elder then the younger; though one dies he still wins prestige, and sons and grandsons will long lead the various states.

sentences.zh: 漢雖強，猶不能兼併匈奴。

translations.literal: Though Han is strong, it still cannot annex and merge the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Though Han is strong, it still cannot annex the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 奈何亂先古之制，臣事於漢，卑辱先單于，為諸國所笑！

translations.literal: How can we disorder the institutions of former antiquity, serve Han as subjects, and humiliate the former Chanyu, becoming what the various states laugh at!
translations.idiomatic: How can we overturn ancient institutions, serve Han as subjects, humiliate the former Chanyu, and become a laughingstock to the various states!

sentences.zh: 雖如是而安，何以復長百蠻！

translations.literal: Even if we were secure thus, how could we again lead the hundred barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: Even if we were secure thus, how could we again lead the hundred barbarians!

sentences.zh: 」左伊秩訾曰：「不然，強弱有時。

translations.literal: " The Left Yizhi Zhi said: "It is not so—strength and weakness have their seasons.
translations.idiomatic: " The Left Yizhi Zhi said, "It is not so—strength and weakness have their seasons.

sentences.zh: 今漢方盛，烏孫城郭諸國皆為臣妾。

translations.literal: Now Han is flourishing; the walled states of Wusun and all the rest have become subjects and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Now Han is flourishing; the walled states of Wusun and all the rest have become Han subjects.

sentences.zh: 自且鞮侯單于以來，匈奴日削，不能取復，雖屈強於此，未嘗一日安也。

translations.literal: From the time of Chanyu Qiedihou onward, the Xiongnu daily dwindled and could not recover; though they bent their strength here, they never had a single day of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Since Chanyu Qiedihou, the Xiongnu have daily dwindled and could not recover; though they bent their strength here, they never had a day of peace.

sentences.zh: 今事漢則安存，不事則危亡，計何以過此！

translations.literal: Now to serve Han is security and survival; not to serve is peril and extinction—what plan surpasses this!
translations.idiomatic: Now to serve Han is security; not to serve is extinction—what plan surpasses this!

sentences.zh: 」諸大人相難久之，呼韓邪從其計，引眾南近塞，遣子右賢王銖婁渠堂入侍。

translations.literal: " The various great men disputed one another for a long time; Huhanye followed his plan, led his masses south near the passes, and sent his son the Right Wise King Zhu Louqu Tang to enter and attend court.
translations.idiomatic: " The great men disputed for a long time; Huhanye followed his plan, led his people south near the border, and sent his son the Right Wise King Zhu Louqu Tang to attend court.

sentences.zh: 郅支單于亦遣子右大將駒于利受入侍。

translations.literal: Chanyu Zhizhi also sent his son the Right Grand General Juyu Lishou to enter and attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Chanyu Zhizhi also sent his son the Right Grand General Juyu Lishou to attend court.

sentences.zh: ----6二月，丁巳，樂成敬侯許延壽薨。

translations.literal: ----6 In the second month, on day dingsi, Marquis Jing of Lecheng Xu Yanshou died.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In the second month, on day dingsi, Marquis Jing of Lecheng Xu Yanshou died.

sentences.zh: ----7夏，四月，黃龍見新豐。

translations.literal: ----7 In summer, the fourth month, a yellow dragon appeared at Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 In summer, the fourth month, a yellow dragon appeared at Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: ----8丙申，太上皇廟火；

translations.literal: ----8 On day bingshen, the Grand Supreme Emperor's temple caught fire;
translations.idiomatic: ----8 On day bingshen, the Grand Supreme Emperor's temple caught fire;

sentences.zh: 甲辰，孝文廟火；

translations.literal: on day jiachen, Emperor Wen's temple caught fire;
translations.idiomatic: on day jiachen, Emperor Wen's temple caught fire;

sentences.zh: 上素服五日。

translations.literal: the emperor wore plain white garments for five days.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor wore plain mourning garments for five days.

sentences.zh: ----9烏孫狂王復尚楚主解憂，生一男鴟靡，不與主和，又暴惡失眾。

translations.literal: ----9 The Mad King of Wusun again took in marriage the Chu princess Jieyou and begot a son, Nimi; he was not harmonious with the princess and again was violent and wicked, losing the masses.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 The Mad King of Wusun again married the Chu princess Jieyou and begot a son, Nimi; he was not harmonious with her and was violent and wicked, losing popular support.

sentences.zh: 漢使衛司馬魏和意、副侯任昌至烏孫。

translations.literal: Han sent Guard Major Wei Heyi and Deputy Marquis Ren Chang to Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent Guard Major Wei Heyi and Deputy Marquis Ren Chang to Wusun.

sentences.zh: 公主言：「狂王為烏孫所患苦，易誅也。

translations.literal: The princess said: "The Mad King is what Wusun suffers from; he is easy to execute.
translations.idiomatic: The princess said, "The Mad King is what Wusun suffers from; he is easy to kill.

sentences.zh: 」遂謀置酒，使士拔劍擊之。

translations.literal: " They thereupon plotted to set out wine and had soldiers draw swords and strike him.
translations.idiomatic: " They plotted a banquet and had soldiers draw swords and strike him.

sentences.zh: 劍旁下，狂王傷，上馬馳去。

translations.literal: The sword struck beside him; the Mad King was wounded, mounted his horse, and galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: The sword struck beside him; the Mad King was wounded, mounted his horse, and fled.

sentences.zh: 其子細沈瘦會兵圍和意、昌及公主於赤谷城。

translations.literal: His son Xishen Sou gathered troops and besieged Heyi, Chang, and the princess at Red Valley City.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xishen Sou gathered troops and besieged Heyi, Chang, and the princess at Red Valley City.

sentences.zh: 數月，都護鄭吉發諸國兵救之，乃解去。

translations.literal: Several months later, Protector-General Zheng Ji mobilized the various states' troops to rescue them, and the siege was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later, Protector-General Zheng Ji mobilized troops from the various states to rescue them, and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 漢遣中郎將張遵持醫藥治狂王，賜金帛。

translations.literal: Han sent Palace Gentleman Zhang Zun bearing medicine to treat the Mad King and bestowed gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent Palace Gentleman Zhang Zun with medicine to treat the Mad King and bestowed gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 因收和意、昌系瑣，從尉犁檻車至長安，斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Heyi and Chang were seized in fetters, sent in a caged cart from Weili to Chang'an, and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Heyi and Chang were seized in fetters, sent in a caged cart from Weili to Chang'an, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 初，肥王翁歸靡胡婦子烏就屠，狂王傷時，驚，與諸翎侯俱去，居北山中，揚言母家匈奴兵來，故眾歸之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Fat King Wengguimi's son by a Hu woman was Wujiutu; when the Mad King was wounded, startled, he went off together with the various commandery lords and dwelt in the northern mountains, proclaiming that his mother's family, the Xiongnu, were coming with troops—therefore the masses turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Fat King Wengguimi's son by a Hu woman was Wujiutu; when the Mad King was wounded, startled, he went off with the various commandery lords and dwelt in the northern mountains, proclaiming that Xiongnu troops from his mother's family were coming—therefore the people turned to him.

sentences.zh: 後遂襲殺狂王，自立為昆彌。

translations.literal: Later he thereupon raided and killed the Mad King and established himself as Kunmi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he raided and killed the Mad King and established himself as Kunmi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漢遣破羌將軍辛武賢將兵萬五千人至敦煌，通渠積穀，欲以討之。

translations.literal: That year, Han sent Break-Qiang General Xin Wuxian to lead fifteen thousand troops to Dunhuang, open canals and store grain, intending thereby to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Han sent Break-Qiang General Xin Wuxian with fifteen thousand troops to Dunhuang to open canals and store grain, intending to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 初，楚主侍者馮嫽，能史書，習事，嘗持漢節為公主使，城郭諸國敬信之，號曰馮夫人，為烏孫右大將妻。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Chu princess's attendant Feng Liao could write histories and was practiced in affairs; she had once held Han credentials as the princess's envoy; the walled states all respected and trusted her and called her Lady Feng; she was wife to Wusun's Right Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Chu princess's attendant Feng Liao could write and was skilled in affairs; she had held Han credentials as the princess's envoy; the walled states respected and trusted her and called her Lady Feng; she was wife to Wusun's Right Grand General.

sentences.zh: 右大將與烏就屠相愛，都護鄭吉使馮夫人說烏就屠，以漢兵方出，必見滅，不如降。

translations.literal: The Right Grand General and Wujiutu were mutually fond; Protector-General Zheng Ji had Lady Feng persuade Wujiutu that Han troops were just going forth and he would surely be destroyed—better to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Grand General and Wujiutu were close; Protector-General Zheng Ji had Lady Feng persuade Wujiutu that Han troops were marching and he would surely be destroyed—better to surrender.

sentences.zh: 烏就屠恐，曰：「願得小號以自處！

translations.literal: Wujiutu was afraid and said: "I wish to obtain a lesser title by which to settle myself!
translations.idiomatic: Wujiutu was afraid and said, "I wish to obtain a lesser title to maintain myself!

sentences.zh: 」帝征馮夫人，自問狀。

translations.literal: " The emperor summoned Lady Feng and himself asked the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor summoned Lady Feng and questioned her himself.

sentences.zh: 遣謁者竺次、期門甘延壽為副，送馮夫人。

translations.literal: He dispatched Usher Zhu Ci and Palace Gate Guard Gan Yanshou as deputies to escort Lady Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Usher Zhu Ci and Palace Gate Guard Gan Yanshou as deputies to escort Lady Feng.

sentences.zh: 馮夫人錦車持節，詔烏就屠詣長羅侯赤谷城，立元貴靡為大昆彌，烏就屠為小昆彌，皆賜印綬。

translations.literal: Lady Feng in a brocade carriage held credentials and ordered Wujiutu to proceed to the Chief Luo Marquis at Red Valley City; Yuan Guimi was established as Great Kunmi, Wujiutu as Lesser Kunmi—both were bestowed seals and cords.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng in a brocade carriage held credentials and ordered Wujiutu to Red Valley City; Yuan Guimi was established as Great Kunmi, Wujiutu as Lesser Kunmi—both received seals and cords.

sentences.zh: 破羌將軍不出塞，還。

translations.literal: The Break-Qiang General did not go beyond the passes and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Break-Qiang General did not cross the border and returned.

sentences.zh: 後烏就屠不盡歸諸翎侯民眾，漢復遣長羅侯將三校屯赤谷，因為分別其人民地界，大昆彌戶六萬餘，小昆彌戶四萬餘。

translations.literal: Later Wujiutu did not fully return the various commandery lords' people and masses; Han again sent the Chief Luo Marquis to lead three garrisons to encamp at Red Valley and thereby divide their people's territorial boundaries—Great Kunmi had more than sixty thousand households, Lesser Kunmi more than forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wujiutu did not fully return the people's masses; Han again sent the Chief Luo Marquis with three garrisons to encamp at Red Valley and divide their territories—Great Kunmi had more than sixty thousand households, Lesser Kunmi more than forty thousand.

sentences.zh: 然眾心皆附小昆彌。

translations.literal: Yet all hearts attached to the Lesser Kunmi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet popular support all attached to the Lesser Kunmi.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，立皇子囂為定陶王。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor's son Biao was established as Prince of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor's son Biao was established as Prince of Dingtao.

sentences.zh: ----2詔赦天下，減民算三十。

translations.literal: ----2 An edict amnestied all under Heaven and reduced the people's poll tax by thirty.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 An edict amnestied all under Heaven and reduced the poll tax by thirty.

sentences.zh: ----3珠崖郡反。

translations.literal: ----3 Zhuya Commandery rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Zhuya Commandery rebelled.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，遣護軍都尉張祿將兵擊之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Colonel of the Guard Zhang Lu was dispatched to lead troops and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Colonel of the Guard Zhang Lu was dispatched with troops to attack them.

sentences.zh: ----4杜延年以老病免。

translations.literal: ----4 Du Yannian was dismissed because of old age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Du Yannian was dismissed because of old age and illness.

sentences.zh: 五月，己丑，廷尉-{于定國}-為御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on day jichou, Director of Justice Yu Dingguo became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on day jichou, Director of Justice Yu Dingguo became Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: ----5秋，九月，立皇子宇為東平王。

translations.literal: ----5 In autumn, the ninth month, the emperor's son Yu was established as Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In autumn, the ninth month, the emperor's son Yu was established as Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: ----6冬，十二月，上行幸萯陽宮、屬玉觀。

translations.literal: ----6 In winter, the twelfth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Fuyang Palace and Jade-Quail View.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In winter, the twelfth month, the emperor traveled to Fuyang Palace and Jade-Quail View.

sentences.zh: ----7是歲，營平壯武侯趙充國薨。

translations.literal: ----7 That year, Marquis Zhuangwu of Yingping Zhao Chongguo died.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 That year, Marquis Zhuangwu of Yingping Zhao Chongguo died.

sentences.zh: 先是，充國以老乞骸骨，賜安車、駟馬、黃金，罷就第。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chongguo because of age requested his bones and was bestowed a secure carriage, four-horse team, and gold, dismissed to return to his estate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chongguo because of age requested retirement and was granted a secure carriage, four-horse team, and gold, then dismissed to his estate.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每有四夷大議，常與參兵謀、問籌策焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had great deliberations on the four Yi, it constantly had him participate in military planning and ask his stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court had major deliberations on the four barbarians, it constantly consulted him on military planning and strategy.

sentences.zh: ----8匈奴呼韓邪單于款五原塞，原奉國珍，朝三年正月。

translations.literal: ----8 The Xiongnu Chanyu Huhanye came in good faith to Wuyuan Pass, wishing to present national treasures and attend court in the first month of the third year.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 The Xiongnu chanyu Huhanye came in good faith to Wuyuan Pass, wishing to present national treasures and attend court in the first month of the third year.

sentences.zh: 詔有司議其儀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate on the ceremonial arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate on the ceremonial arrangements.

sentences.zh: 丞相、御史曰：「聖王之制，先京師而後諸夏，先諸夏而後夷狄。

translations.literal: The chancellor and censor-in-chief said: "The sage king's system puts the capital first, then the various Xia; the various Xia first, then the Yi and Di.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor and censor-in-chief said, "The sage king's system puts the capital first, then the various Xia; the various Xia first, then the Yi and Di."

sentences.zh: 匈奴單于朝賀，其禮儀宜如諸侯王，位次在下。

translations.literal: When the Xiongnu chanyu comes to court for congratulations, his ceremonial observances should be like those of feudal kings, with his place in rank below them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiongnu chanyu comes to court for congratulations, his ceremonial observances should be like those of feudal kings, with his place in rank below them.

sentences.zh: 」太子太傅蕭望之以為：「單于非正朔所加，故稱敵國，宜待以不臣之禮，位在諸侯王上。

translations.literal: " The tutor of the heir apparent Xiao Wangzhi held: "The chanyu is not one upon whom the correct calendar was conferred; he is therefore called a rival state. He should be received with the ritual due one who is not a subject, with rank above the feudal kings.
translations.idiomatic: " Tutor of the Heir Apparent Xiao Wangzhi argued, "The chanyu is not one upon whom the correct calendar was conferred; he is therefore called a rival state. He should be received with the ritual due one who is not a subject, with rank above the feudal kings."

sentences.zh: 外夷稽首稱籓，中國讓而不臣，此則羈縻之誼，謙亨之福也。

translations.literal: The outer Yi bow and call themselves vassals; the Central States yield and do not make them subjects—this is the meaning of bridling and tying, the fortune of humble attainment.
translations.idiomatic: The outer barbarians bow and call themselves vassals; the Central States yield and do not make them subjects—this is the meaning of keeping them on loose reins, the fortune of modest forbearance.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『戎狄荒服，』言其來服荒忽亡常。

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'The Rong and Di are wild-domain tribute,' meaning that they come to submit in wildness, suddenly appearing and vanishing without constancy.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "The Rong and Di are wild-domain tribute," meaning that they come to submit from distant lands, suddenly appearing and vanishing without constancy.

sentences.zh: 如使匈奴後嗣卒有鳥竄鼠伏，闕於朝享，不為畔臣，萬世之長策也。

translations.literal: If the Xiongnu's later generations in the end scurry like birds and hide like rats, fail in court attendance, yet are not rebellious subjects—that is a long-range policy for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: If the Xiongnu's later generations in the end scurry like birds and hide like rats, fail in court attendance, yet are not treated as rebellious subjects—that is a long-range policy for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 」天子采之，下詔曰：「匈奴單于稱北蕃，朝正朔。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven adopted this and issued an edict: "The Xiongnu chanyu calls himself the northern藩 and attends the correct calendar.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor adopted this and issued an edict: "The Xiongnu chanyu calls himself the northern藩 and attends the correct calendar."

sentences.zh: 朕之不德，不能弘覆。

translations.literal: My lack of virtue cannot broadly cover all.
translations.idiomatic: My lack of virtue cannot broadly shelter all.

sentences.zh: 其以客禮待之，令單于位在諸侯王上，贊謁稱臣而不名。

translations.literal: Let him be received with guest ritual; order the chanyu's place above the feudal kings; at presentation let him be called subject but not by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be received with guest ritual; place the chanyu above the feudal kings; at presentation let him be called subject but not by personal name.

sentences.zh: :荀悅論曰：《春秋》之義，王者無外，欲一於天下也。

translations.literal: : Xun Yue's discussion says: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that the king has no outside—he wishes oneness in All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: : Xun Yue's discussion says: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that the king has no outside—he wishes oneness in All-under-Heaven.

sentences.zh: 戎狄道理遼遠，人跡介絕，故正朔不及，禮教不加，非尊之也，其勢然也。

translations.literal: The Rong and Di lie on roads distant and far, human traces cut off; therefore the correct calendar does not reach them and ritual teaching is not applied—not because they are honored, but because the situation is so.
translations.idiomatic: The Rong and Di lie on roads distant and far, human traces cut off; therefore the correct calendar does not reach them and ritual teaching is not applied—not because they are honored, but because the situation is so.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「自彼氐、羌，莫敢不來王。

translations.literal: The Odes says: "From those Di and Qiang, none dares not come to court as king [tributary].
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, "From those Di and Qiang, none dares fail to come to court."

sentences.zh: 」故要、荒之君必奉王貢。

translations.literal: " Therefore lords of the yao and huang domains must present royal tribute.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore lords of the outer and wild domains must present royal tribute.

sentences.zh: 若不供職，則有辭讓號令加焉，非敵國之謂也。

translations.literal: If they do not perform their duties, then words of reproof and orders and commands are applied to them—not the meaning of rival state.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not perform their duties, reproof and orders are applied to them—they are not called rival states.

sentences.zh: 望之欲待以不臣之禮，加之王公之上，僭度失序，以亂天常，非禮也！

translations.literal: Wangzhi wishing to receive him with the ritual of one not a subject and place him above kings and dukes transgresses degrees, loses order, and disorders the heavenly constancy—it is not ritual!
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi's wish to receive him with the ritual of one not a subject and place him above kings and dukes transgresses proper rank, destroys order, and disorders the heavenly constancy—it is not ritual!

sentences.zh: 若以權時之宜，則異論矣。

translations.literal: If judged by the expedient fit of the time, then it is a different discussion.
translations.idiomatic: If judged by the expedient fit of the time, then it is a different matter.

sentences.zh: ----9詔遣車騎都尉韓昌迎單于，發所過七郡二千騎為陳道上。

translations.literal: ----9 An edict sent Commandant of Cavalry Han Chang to welcome the chanyu and dispatched two thousand cavalry from the seven commanderies along the route to form an escort on the road.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 An edict sent Commandant of Cavalry Han Chang to welcome the chanyu and dispatched two thousand cavalry from the seven commanderies along the route to escort him on the road.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，上行幸甘泉，郊泰畤。

translations.literal: 1 Spring, first month, the emperor travelled in favor to Ganquan and performed suburban sacrifice at Tai畤.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor travelled to Ganquan and performed suburban sacrifice at Tai畤.

sentences.zh: ----2匈奴呼韓邪單于來朝，贊謁稱籓臣而不名。

translations.literal: ----2 The Xiongnu Chanyu Huhanye came to court; at presentation he was called a vassal subject but not by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 The Xiongnu chanyu Huhanye came to court; at presentation he was called a vassal subject but not by personal name.

sentences.zh: 賜以冠帶、衣裳，黃金璽、盭綬，玉具劍、佩刀，弓一張，矢四發，棨戟十，安車一乘，鞍勒一具，馬十五匹，黃金二十斤，錢二十萬，衣被七十七襲，錦繡、綺縠、雜帛八千匹，絮六千斤。

translations.literal: He was granted cap and belt, robes, a golden seal and盭 ribbon, a jade-fitted sword and girdle knife, one bow, four arrows in a quiver, ten halberds with tassels, one cushioned carriage, one set of saddle and bridle, fifteen horses, twenty jin of gold, two hundred thousand cash, seventy-seven suits of clothing and coverlets, eight thousand bolts of brocade, damask, fine silk, and miscellaneous silks, and six thousand jin of wadding.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted cap and belt, robes, a golden seal and盭 ribbon, a jade-fitted sword and girdle knife, one bow, four arrows in a quiver, ten halberds with tassels, one cushioned carriage, one set of saddle and bridle, fifteen horses, twenty jin of gold, two hundred thousand cash, seventy-seven suits of clothing and coverlets, eight thousand bolts of brocade, damask, fine silk, and miscellaneous silks, and six thousand jin of wadding.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，使使者道單于先行宿長平。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, the emperor sent an envoy to escort the chanyu ahead to lodge at Changping.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, the emperor sent an envoy to escort the chanyu ahead to lodge at Changping.

sentences.zh: 上自甘泉宿池陽宮。

translations.literal: The emperor himself, coming from Ganquan, lodged at Chiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself, coming from Ganquan, lodged at Chiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 上登長平阪，詔單于毋謁，其左右當戶群臣皆得列觀，及諸蠻夷君長、王、侯數萬，咸迎於渭橋下，夾道陳。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended Changping Slope and ordered that the chanyu need not pay audience; his attendants and the Household ministers at the gate all could stand in ranks to observe, and several tens of thousands of various barbarian chieftains, kings, and marquises all welcomed him below Wei Bridge, arrayed along both sides of the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended Changping Slope and ordered that the chanyu need not pay audience; his attendants and the Household ministers at the gate all could stand in ranks to observe, and several tens of thousands of various barbarian chieftains, kings, and marquises all welcomed him below Wei Bridge, arrayed along both sides of the road.

sentences.zh: 上登渭橋，咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted Wei Bridge; all called "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted Wei Bridge; all cried "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 單于就邸長安。

translations.literal: The chanyu arrived at his lodge in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu arrived at his lodge in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 置酒建章宮，饗賜單于，觀以珍寶。

translations.literal: Wine was set out at Jianzhang Palace; the chanyu was feasted and gifted, and shown precious treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was set out at Jianzhang Palace; the chanyu was feasted and gifted, and shown precious treasures.

sentences.zh: 二月，遣單于歸國。

translations.literal: Second month, the chanyu was sent home to his state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the chanyu was sent home to his state.

sentences.zh: 單于自請「願留居幕南光祿塞下；

translations.literal: The chanyu himself requested: "I wish to remain dwelling south of the curtain below Guanglu Pass;
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu himself requested, "I wish to remain dwelling south of the curtain below Guanglu Pass;"

sentences.zh: 有急，保漢受降城。

translations.literal: if there is an emergency, I may take refuge at the Han Surrender-Accepting Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: if there is an emergency, I may take refuge at the Han Surrender-Accepting Fortress."

sentences.zh: 」漢遣長樂衛尉、高昌侯董忠、車騎都尉韓昌將騎萬六千，又發邊郡士馬以千數，送單于出朔方雞鹿塞。

translations.literal: " The Han sent Chief Commandant of Changle Wei Dong Zhong, Marquis of Gaochang, and Commandant of Cavalry Han Chang leading sixteen thousand cavalry, and also raised border commandery troops and horses by the thousands, to escort the chanyu out through Shuofang's Jilu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: " The Han sent Chief Commandant of Changle Wei Dong Zhong, Marquis of Gaochang, and Commandant of Cavalry Han Chang leading sixteen thousand cavalry, and also raised border commandery troops and horses by the thousands, to escort the chanyu out through Shuofang's Jilu Pass.

sentences.zh: 詔忠等留衛單于，助誅不服，又轉邊谷米糒，前後三萬四千斛，給贍其食。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Dong and the others to remain and guard the chanyu, help punish those who would not submit, and also forwarded border-grain rice and dried grain—thirty-four thousand hu in all—to supply his food.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Dong and the others to remain and guard the chanyu, help punish those who would not submit, and also forwarded border-grain rice and dried grain—thirty-four thousand hu in all—to supply his food.

sentences.zh: 先是，自烏孫以西至安息諸國近匈奴者，皆畏匈奴而輕漢，及呼韓邪單于朝漢後，咸尊漢矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, from Wusun west to Parthia, all states near the Xiongnu feared the Xiongnu and slighted the Han; after Chanyu Huhanye attended the Han court, all honored the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, from Wusun west to Parthia, all states near the Xiongnu feared the Xiongnu and slighted the Han; after Chanyu Huhanye attended the Han court, all honored the Han.

sentences.zh: 上以戎狄賓服，思股肱之美，乃圖畫其人於麒麟閣，法其容貌，署其官爵、姓名。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the Rong and Di had come as guests and submitted, thought of the beauty of his chief ministers and therefore painted their likenesses in Qilin Pavilion, taking their appearances as models and inscribing their offices, ranks, and names.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Rong and Di had come as guests and submitted, the emperor thought of the worth of his chief ministers and had their likenesses painted in Qilin Pavilion, modeled on their appearances, with their offices, ranks, and names inscribed.

sentences.zh: 唯霍光不名，曰「大司馬、大將軍、博陸候，姓霍氏」。

translations.literal: Only Huo Guang was not named by personal name; it read "Grand Marshal, Grand General, Marquis of Bolu, surname Huo."
translations.idiomatic: Only Huo Guang was not named by personal name; the inscription read "Grand Marshal, Grand General, Marquis of Bolu, surname Huo."

sentences.zh: 其次張安世、韓增、趙充國、魏相、丙吉、杜延年、劉德、梁丘賀、蕭望之、蘇武。

translations.literal: Next came Zhang Anshi, Han Zeng, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Du Yannian, Liu De, Liangqiu He, Xiao Wangzhi, and Su Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Zhang Anshi, Han Zeng, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Du Yannian, Liu De, Liangqiu He, Xiao Wangzhi, and Su Wu.

sentences.zh: 凡十一人，皆有功德，知名當世，是以表而揚之，明著中興輔佐，列於方叔、召虎、仲山甫焉。

translations.literal: Eleven in all had merit and achievement and were renowned in their age; therefore they were displayed and exalted, clearly showing the restoration-era assistants, ranked with Fang Shu, Duke of Shao, and Zhong Shanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven in all had merit and achievement and were renowned in their age; therefore they were displayed and exalted, clearly showing the restoration-era assistants, ranked with Fang Shu, Duke of Shao, and Zhong Shanfu.

sentences.zh: ----3鳳皇集新蔡。

translations.literal: ----3 A phoenix gathered at Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 A phoenix gathered at Xincai.

sentences.zh: ----4三月，己巳、建成安侯黃霸薨。

translations.literal: ----4 Third month, on jisi, Marquis An of Jiancheng Huang Ba passed away.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the third month, on jisi, Marquis An of Jiancheng Huang Ba died.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲午，-{于定國}-為丞相，封西平侯。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on jiawu, -{Yu Dingguo}- became chancellor and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiawu, -{Yu Dingguo}- became chancellor and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 太僕沛郡陳萬年為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Stud Chen Wannian of Pei Commandery became censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Stud Chen Wannian of Pei Commandery became censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: ----5詔諸儒講五經同異，蕭望之等平奏其議，上帝稱制臨決焉。

translations.literal: ----5 An edict ordered the various Confucians to discuss the agreements and differences of the Five Classics; Xiao Wangzhi and others fairly reported their deliberations, and the emperor personally decided by imperial pronouncement.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 An edict ordered the various Confucians to discuss the agreements and differences of the Five Classics; Xiao Wangzhi and others fairly reported their deliberations, and the emperor personally decided by imperial pronouncement.

sentences.zh: 乃立梁丘《易》、大、小夏侯《尚書》、《穀梁春秋》博士。

translations.literal: Thereupon erudites were established for Liangqiu's Changes, the Great and Little Xiahou Documents, and the Guliang Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon erudites were established for Liangqiu's Changes, the Great and Little Xiahou Documents, and the Guliang Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: ----6烏孫大昆彌元貴靡及鴟靡皆病死。

translations.literal: ----6 Wusun Great Kunmi Yuan Guimie and Chimi both died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 Wusun Great Kunmi Yuan Guimie and Chimi both died of illness.

sentences.zh: 公主上書言：「年老土思，願得歸骸骨，葬漢地！

translations.literal: The princess submitted a memorial saying: "I am old and homesick for my native soil; I wish to have my bones returned and buried in Han territory!
translations.idiomatic: The princess submitted a memorial saying, "I am old and homesick for my native soil; I wish to have my bones returned and buried in Han territory!"

sentences.zh: 」天子閔而迎之。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven pitied her and welcomed her back.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor pitied her and welcomed her back.

sentences.zh: 冬，至京師，待之一如公主之制。

translations.literal: Winter, she reached the capital and was treated entirely according to princess rites.
translations.idiomatic: In winter she reached the capital and was treated entirely according to princess rites.

sentences.zh: 後二歲卒。

translations.literal: Two years later she died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later she died.

sentences.zh: ----7元貴靡子星靡代為大昆彌，弱。

translations.literal: ----7 Yuan Guimie's son Xingmie succeeded as Great Kunmi; he was weak.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 Yuan Guimie's son Xingmie succeeded as Great Kunmi; he was weak.

sentences.zh: 馮夫人上書：「願使烏孫，鎮撫星靡。

translations.literal: Lady Feng submitted a memorial: "I wish to be sent to Wusun to pacify and comfort Xingmie.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng submitted a memorial: "I wish to be sent to Wusun to pacify and comfort Xingmie."

sentences.zh: 」漢遣之。

translations.literal: " The Han sent her.
translations.idiomatic: " The Han sent her.

sentences.zh: 都護韓宣奏烏孫大吏大祿、大監皆可賜以金印紫綬，以尊輔大昆彌。

translations.literal: Protector General Han Xuan memorialized that Wusun's great administrator Dalu and great supervisor could both be granted gold seals and purple ribbons to honor and assist the Great Kunmi.
translations.idiomatic: Protector General Han Xuan memorialized that Wusun's great administrator Dalu and great supervisor could both be granted gold seals and purple ribbons to honor and assist the Great Kunmi.

sentences.zh: 漢許之。

translations.literal: The Han granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Han granted this.

sentences.zh: 其後段會宗為都護，乃招還亡叛，安定之。

translations.literal: Afterward Duan Huizong became protector general; he then summoned back deserters and rebels and pacified the state.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Duan Huizong became protector general; he then summoned back deserters and rebels and pacified the state.

sentences.zh: 星靡死，子雌栗靡代立。

translations.literal: Xingmie died; his son Ciliqimie succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmie died; his son Ciliqimie succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: ----8皇太子所幸司馬良娣病，且死，謂太子曰：「妾死非天命，乃諸娣妾、良人更祝詛殺我。

translations.literal: ----8 The crown prince's favored Lady of the Chief of Cavalry Liang was ill and near death; she told the crown prince: "My death is not Heaven's decree—it is the various secondary consorts and ladies who by turns prayed and cursed me to death.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 The crown prince's favored Lady of the Chief of Cavalry Liang was ill and near death; she told the crown prince, "My death is not Heaven's decree—it is the various secondary consorts and ladies who by turns prayed and cursed me to death."

sentences.zh: 」太子以為然。

translations.literal: " The crown prince believed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince believed it.

sentences.zh: 及死，太子悲恚發病，忽忽不樂。

translations.literal: When she died, the crown prince grieved and fell ill, restless and joyless.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, the crown prince grieved and fell ill, restless and joyless.

sentences.zh: 帝乃令皇后擇後宮家人子可以娛侍太子者，得元城王政君，送太子宮。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the empress to choose from the palace women of good family one who could divert and attend the crown prince; Wang Zhengjun of Yuancheng was obtained and sent to the crown prince's palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the empress to choose from the palace women of good family one who could divert and attend the crown prince; Wang Zhengjun of Yuancheng was obtained and sent to the crown prince's palace.

sentences.zh: 政君，故繡衣御史賀之孫女也，見於丙殿。

translations.literal: Zhengjun was the granddaughter of the former Embroidered-Robe Censor He and had been seen in the Bing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengjun was the granddaughter of the former Embroidered-Robe Censor He and had been seen in the Bing Hall.

sentences.zh: 壹幸，有身。

translations.literal: Once favored, she became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: Once favored, she became pregnant.

sentences.zh: 是歲，生成帝於甲館畫堂，為世縕皇孫。

translations.literal: That year she gave birth to Emperor Cheng in the Painted Hall of the Jia Lodge; he was made heir-apparent great-grandson in the womb belt.
translations.idiomatic: That year she gave birth to Emperor Cheng in the Painted Hall of the Jia Lodge; he was made heir-apparent great-grandson in the womb belt.

sentences.zh: 帝愛之，自名曰驁，字大孫，常置左右。

translations.literal: The emperor loved him, personally named him Ao, styled Dasun, and often kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved him, personally named him Ao, styled Dasun, and often kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 1夏，廣川王海陽坐禽獸行、賊殺不辜，廢，徙房陵。

translations.literal: 1 Summer, King Haiyang of Guangchuan was charged with beastlike conduct and murdering the innocent; he was deposed and moved to Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In summer, King Haiyang of Guangchuan was charged with beastlike conduct and murdering the innocent; he was deposed and moved to Fangling.

sentences.zh: ----2冬，十月，丁卯，未央宮宣室閣火。

translations.literal: ----2 Winter, tenth month, on dingmao, the Xuanshi Pavilion of Weiyang Palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In winter, the tenth month, on dingmao, the Xuanshi Pavilion of Weiyang Palace caught fire.

sentences.zh: ----3是歲，徙定陶王囂為楚王。

translations.literal: ----3 That year, King Xiao of Dingtao was moved to become King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 That year, King Xiao of Dingtao was moved to become King of Chu.

sentences.zh: ----4匈奴呼韓邪、郅支兩單于俱遣使朝獻，漢待呼韓邪使有加焉。

translations.literal: ----4 Both the Xiongnu chanyus Huhanye and Zhizhi sent envoys with tribute to court; the Han treated Huhanye's envoy with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Both the Xiongnu chanyus Huhanye and Zhizhi sent envoys with tribute to court; the Han treated Huhanye's envoy with special favor.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，上行幸甘泉，郊泰畤。

translations.literal: 1 Spring, first month, the emperor travelled in favor to Ganquan and performed suburban sacrifice at Tai畤.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor travelled to Ganquan and performed suburban sacrifice at Tai畤.

sentences.zh: ----2匈奴呼韓邪單于來朝；

translations.literal: ----2 The Xiongnu Chanyu Huhanye came to court;
translations.idiomatic: ----2 The Xiongnu chanyu Huhanye came to court;

sentences.zh: 二月，歸國。

translations.literal: second month, he returned to his state.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month he returned to his state.

sentences.zh: 始，郅支單于以為呼韓邪兵弱，降漢，不能復自還，即引其眾西，欲攻定右地。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Chanyu Zhizhi thought Huhanye's troops were weak, that having submitted to the Han he could not return on his own; he therefore led his masses west, intending to attack and secure the right territory.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, Chanyu Zhizhi thought Huhanye's troops were weak and that, having submitted to the Han, he could not return on his own; he therefore led his followers west, intending to attack and secure the right territory.

sentences.zh: 又屠耆單于小弟本侍呼韓邪，亦亡之右地，收兩兄餘兵，得數千人，自立為伊利目單于；

translations.literal: Also the younger brother of Chanyu Rizhi, who had originally served Huhanye, also fled to the right territory, gathered the remnant troops of his two elder brothers, obtained several thousand men, and established himself as Chanyu Yilimu;
translations.idiomatic: Also the younger brother of Chanyu Rizhi, who had originally served Huhanye, also fled to the right territory, gathered the remnant troops of his two elder brothers, obtained several thousand men, and established himself as Chanyu Yilimu;

sentences.zh: 道逢郅支，合戰，郅支殺之，併其兵五萬餘人。

translations.literal: on the road he met Zhizhi; they joined battle, Zhizhi killed him, and merged his troops to more than fifty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: on the road he met Zhizhi; they joined battle, Zhizhi killed him, and merged his troops to more than fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 郅支聞漢出兵谷助呼韓邪，即遂留居右地；

translations.literal: Zhizhi heard the Han had sent troops through the valley to help Huhanye and thereupon remained dwelling in the right territory;
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi heard the Han had sent troops through the valley to help Huhanye and thereupon remained dwelling in the right territory;

sentences.zh: 自度力不能定匈奴，乃益西，近烏孫，欲與並力，遣使見小昆彌烏就屠。

translations.literal: judging for himself that his strength could not settle the Xiongnu, he went further west, drew near Wusun, wished to combine forces, and sent an envoy to see the Little Kunmi Wujiutu.
translations.idiomatic: judging for himself that his strength could not settle the Xiongnu, he went further west, drew near Wusun, wished to combine forces, and sent an envoy to see the Little Kunmi Wujiutu.

sentences.zh: 烏就屠殺其使，發八千騎迎郅支。

translations.literal: Wujiutu killed his envoy and sent eight thousand cavalry to welcome Zhizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wujiutu killed his envoy and sent eight thousand cavalry to welcome Zhizhi.

sentences.zh: 郅支覺其謀，勒兵逢擊烏孫，破之；

translations.literal: Zhizhi perceived the plot, led his troops to meet and strike Wusun, and broke them;
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi perceived the plot, led his troops to meet and strike Wusun, and defeated them;

sentences.zh: 因北擊烏揭、堅昆、丁令、並三國。

translations.literal: thereupon he struck north against the Wujie, Jiankun, and Dingling and annexed the three states.
translations.idiomatic: thereupon he struck north against the Wujie, Jiankun, and Dingling and annexed the three states.

sentences.zh: 數遣兵擊烏孫，常勝之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent troops to attack Wusun and was often victorious.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sent troops to attack Wusun and was often victorious.

sentences.zh: 堅昆東去單于庭七千里，南去車師五千里，郅支留都之。

translations.literal: Jiankun lay seven thousand li east of the chanyu court and five thousand li south of Cheshi; Zhizhi remained and made it his capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankun lay seven thousand li east of the chanyu court and five thousand li south of Cheshi; Zhizhi remained and made it his capital.

sentences.zh: ----3三月，有星孛於王良、閣道，入紫微宮。

translations.literal: ----3 Third month, a comet appeared at Wangliang and Jiandao and entered the Purple Forbidden Palace.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the third month, a comet appeared at Wangliang and Jiandao and entered the Purple Forbidden Palace.

sentences.zh: ----4帝寢疾，選大臣可屬者，引外屬侍中樂陵侯史高、太子太傅蕭望之、少傅周堪至禁中，拜高為大司馬、車騎將軍，望之為前將軍、光祿勳，堪為光祿大夫，皆受遺詔輔政，領尚書事。

translations.literal: ----4 The emperor lay ill in bed and chose ministers to whom he could entrust affairs; he summoned the related-by-marriage Attendant-in-Ordinary Marquis of Leling Shi Gao, tutor of the heir apparent Xiao Wangzhi, and junior tutor Zhou Kan to the inner palace, appointed Gao grand marshal and general of chariots and cavalry, Wangzhi forward general and director of the imperial secretariat, and Kan director of the masters of writing—all received the testamentary edict to assist in government and headed Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 The emperor lay gravely ill and chose ministers to whom he could entrust affairs; he summoned the related-by-marriage Attendant-in-Ordinary Marquis of Leling Shi Gao, Tutor of the Heir Apparent Xiao Wangzhi, and Junior Tutor Zhou Kan to the inner palace, appointed Gao grand marshal and general of chariots and cavalry, Wangzhi forward general and director of the imperial secretariat, and Kan director of the masters of writing—all received the testamentary edict to assist in government and headed Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，甲戌，帝崩於未央宮。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, on jiaxu, the emperor died at Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, on jiaxu, the emperor died at Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: :班固贊曰：孝宣之治，信賞必罰，綜核名實。

translations.literal: : Ban Gu's praise says: The governance of Emperor Xiaoxuan—rewards and punishments were sure, names and realities were comprehensively verified.
translations.idiomatic: : Ban Gu's praise says: The governance of Emperor Xiaoxuan—rewards and punishments were sure, names and realities were comprehensively verified.

sentences.zh: 政事、文學、法理之士，鹹精其能。

translations.literal: Men of government affairs, letters, and legal principle all refined their abilities.
translations.idiomatic: Men of government affairs, letters, and legal principle all refined their abilities.

sentences.zh: 至於技巧、工匠、器械，自元、成間鮮能及之。

translations.literal: As for skill, craftsmen, and instruments—from the Yuan and Cheng reigns few could match it.
translations.idiomatic: As for skill, craftsmen, and instruments—from the Yuan and Cheng reigns few could match it.

sentences.zh: 亦足以知吏稱其職，民安其業也。

translations.literal: This too is enough to know that officials claimed their posts and the people were secure in their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: This too is enough to know that officials claimed their posts and the people were secure in their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 遭值匈奴乖亂，推亡固存，信威北夷，單于慕義，稽首稱籓。

translations.literal: He encountered the Xiongnu in disorder, pushed the perishing and secured what remained, his trust and might reached the northern Yi; the chanyu admired his righteousness and bowed, calling himself vassal.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered the Xiongnu in disorder, pushed the perishing and secured what remained, his trust and might reached the northern Yi; the chanyu admired his righteousness and bowed, calling himself vassal.

sentences.zh: 功光祖宗，業垂後嗣，可謂中興，侔德殷宗、周宣矣！

translations.literal: His merit illumined the ancestors and his enterprise hangs for posterity; it can be called a restoration, equal in virtue to the Yin Ancestor and King Xuan of Zhou!
translations.idiomatic: His merit illumined the ancestors and his enterprise hangs for posterity; it can be called a restoration, equal in virtue to the Yin Ancestor and King Xuan of Zhou!

sentences.zh: ----5癸巳，太子即皇帝位，謁高廟，尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: ----5 On guisi, the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, visited Gaozu's temple, and honored the empress dowager as Grand Empress Dowager and the empress as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 On guisi, the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, visited Gaozu's temple, and honored the empress dowager as Grand Empress Dowager and the empress as Empress Dowager.
